The problem with answering your question is that I assume by "what happened" you are asking how they did and what the effect of that will be. It is hard to say what it means to "win" a political debate like this. Normal rules of debate don't really count. It's not as though judges award points and the person with the most points takes home a first place prize. The only real metric for these debates is how it affects the candidates standing with voters. That being the case, I don't think anything much of note happened last night.

Trump seemed to do better than Hillary for the first half hour or so and Hillary did better for the rest of the debate. More critically, though, neither really crashed and burned. So I'd say it made no difference to people already leaning one way or the other. People leaning one way or the other probably found what they needed to move them closer to their candidate. For people truly on the fence? They probably are still there.
